informal_statement: There exists a subset $x$ such that for any elements $a$ and $b$, the membership of $op\ h\gamma\ h\delta\ a\ b$ in $x$ under the partial order $h\beta$ is equivalent to $b$ being a subset of $a$ under the relation $h\epsilon$.
informal_proof:
We aim to show that there exists a subset $x$ with the following property: for any $a$ and $b$, $op\ h\gamma\ h\delta\ a\ b \in[ h\beta ] x$ if and only if for every $c$, $c \in[ h\epsilon ] a$ implies $c \in[ h\epsilon ] b$.

To establish the existence of such a subset, we consider the symmetric construction of $y$ and demonstrate its suitability. 

First, we assume that $op\ h\gamma\ h\delta\ a\ b \in[ h\beta ] y$. By the construction of $y$, this implies the existence of $b'$ and $c$ such that $op\ h\gamma\ h\delta\ b' c$ equals $op\ h\gamma\ h\delta\ a\ b$, and for all $c$, if $c \in[ h\epsilon ] b'$ then $c \in[ h\epsilon ] c$. Simplifying, this leads directly to the conclusion that $b$ is a subset of $a$ under $h\epsilon$.

Conversely, if $b$ is a subset of $a$ under $h\epsilon$, we can construct $y$ using $a$ and $b$, ensuring that $op\ h\gamma\ h\delta\ a\ b \in[ h\beta ] y$. This construction preserves the subset property, thereby satisfying the equivalence condition.

The proof also accounts for the behavior under transformations, demonstrating that the constructed subset $y$ maintains its properties under operations involving an automorphism $\rho$. This ensures that the equivalence holds not only in the original structure but also in related transformed structures, thereby confirming the robustness of the subset definition.

Thus, we have established the existence of the required subset $x$ with the desired properties.

open Cardinal Ordinal

namespace ConNF

variable [Params.{u}] {α β γ δ ε ζ : Λ} (hβ : (β : TypeIndex) < α) (hγ : (γ : TypeIndex) < β)
  (hδ : (δ : TypeIndex) < γ) (hε : (ε : TypeIndex) < δ) (hζ : (ζ : TypeIndex) < ε)

namespace TSet

theorem exists_inter (x y : TSet α) :
    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {z | z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := symmetric y hβ
  use S + T
  intro ρ hρ
  specialize hS ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS hT ⊢
  aesop

theorem exists_compl (x : TSet α) :
    ∃ y : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] y ↔ ¬z ∈[hβ] x := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {z | ¬z ∈[hβ] x} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ
  use S
  intro ρ hρ
  specialize hS ρ hρ
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS ⊢
  aesop

theorem exists_up (x y : TSet β) :
    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z = x ∨ z = y := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {x, y} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_support x
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := exists_support y
  use (S + T) ↗ hβ
  intro ρ hρ
  rw [Support.smul_scoderiv, Support.scoderiv_inj, ← allPermSderiv_forget'] at hρ
  specialize hS (ρ ↘ hβ) (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT (ρ ↘ hβ) (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
    exists_eq_or_imp, hS, exists_eq_left, hT]
  ext z
  rw [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  aesop

/-- The unordered pair. -/
def up (x y : TSet β) : TSet α :=
  (exists_up hβ x y).choose

@[simp]
theorem mem_up_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    z ∈[hβ] up hβ x y ↔ z = x ∨ z = y :=
  (exists_up hβ x y).choose_spec z

/-- The Kuratowski ordered pair. -/
def op (x y : TSet γ) : TSet α :=
  up hβ (singleton hγ x) (up hγ x y)

theorem up_injective {x y z w : TSet β} (h : up hβ x y = up hβ z w) :
    (x = z ∧ y = w) ∨ (x = w ∧ y = z) := by
  have h₁ := mem_up_iff hβ x y z
  have h₂ := mem_up_iff hβ x y w
  have h₃ := mem_up_iff hβ z w x
  have h₄ := mem_up_iff hβ z w y
  rw [h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
  rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₃ h₄
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_inj (x y z w : TSet β) :
    up hβ x y = up hβ z w ↔ (x = z ∧ y = w) ∨ (x = w ∧ y = z) := by
  constructor
  · exact up_injective hβ
  · rintro (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
    · rfl
    · apply tSet_ext' hβ
      aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_self {x : TSet β} :
    up hβ x x = singleton hβ x := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_eq_singleton_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    up hβ x y = singleton hβ z ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h₁ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z x
    have h₂ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z y
    rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
    aesop
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rw [up_self]

@[simp]
theorem singleton_eq_up_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    singleton hβ z = up hβ x y ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  rw [← up_eq_singleton_iff hβ x y z, eq_comm]

theorem op_injective {x y z w : TSet γ} (h : op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ z w) :
    x = z ∧ y = w := by
  rw [op, op] at h
  simp only [up_inj, singleton_inj, singleton_eq_up_iff, up_eq_singleton_iff] at h
  obtain (⟨rfl, ⟨h, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨h, rfl⟩⟩) := h <;> simp only [and_self]

@[simp]
theorem op_inj (x y z w : TSet γ) :
    op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ z w ↔ x = z ∧ y = w := by
  constructor
  · exact op_injective hβ hγ
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rfl

@[simp]
theorem op_eq_singleton_iff (x y : TSet γ) (z : TSet β) :
    op hβ hγ x y = singleton hβ z ↔ singleton hγ x = z ∧ singleton hγ y = z := by
  rw [op, up_eq_singleton_iff, and_congr_right_iff]
  rintro rfl
  simp only [up_eq_singleton_iff, true_and, singleton_inj]

@[simp]
theorem smul_up (x y : TSet β) (ρ : AllPerm α) :
    ρ • up hβ x y = up hβ (ρ ↘ hβ • x) (ρ ↘ hβ • y) := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem smul_op (x y : TSet γ) (ρ : AllPerm α) :
    ρ • op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ (ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ • x) (ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ • y) := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  simp only [op, smul_up, smul_singleton, mem_up_iff, implies_true]

theorem exists_singletonImage (x : TSet β) :
    ∃ y : TSet α, ∀ z w,
    op hγ hδ (singleton hε z) (singleton hε w) ∈[hβ] y ↔ op hδ hε z w ∈[hγ] x := by
  have := exists_of_symmetric {u | ∃ z w : TSet ε, op hδ hε z w ∈[hγ] x ∧
      u = op hγ hδ (singleton hε z) (singleton hε w)} hβ ?_
  · obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := this
    use y
    intro z w
    rw [hy]
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, op_inj, singleton_inj, exists_eq_right_right', exists_eq_right']
  · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_support x
    use S ↗ hβ
    intro ρ hρ
    rw [Support.smul_scoderiv, Support.scoderiv_inj, ← allPermSderiv_forget'] at hρ
    specialize hS (ρ ↘ hβ) hρ
    ext z
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, ⟨z, w, hab, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε • z, ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε • w, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rwa [← hS, mem_smul_iff', smul_op, allPerm_inv_sderiv', allPerm_inv_sderiv',
          allPerm_inv_sderiv', inv_smul_smul, inv_smul_smul]
      · simp only [smul_op, smul_singleton]
    · rintro ⟨z, w, hab, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨ρ⁻¹ ↘ hβ • op hγ hδ (singleton hε z) (singleton hε w), ?_, ?_⟩
      · simp only [allPerm_inv_sderiv', smul_op, smul_singleton, Set.mem_setOf_eq, op_inj,
          singleton_inj, exists_eq_right_right', exists_eq_right']
        rw [smul_eq_iff_eq_inv_smul] at hS
        rw [hS]
        simp only [mem_smul_iff', inv_inv, smul_op, smul_inv_smul]
        exact hab
      · simp only [allPerm_inv_sderiv', smul_inv_smul]

theorem exists_insertion2 (x : TSet γ) :
    ∃ y : TSet α, ∀ a b c, op hγ hδ (singleton hε (singleton hζ a)) (op hε hζ b c) ∈[hβ] y ↔
    op hε hζ a c ∈[hδ] x := by
  have := exists_of_symmetric {u | ∃ a b c : TSet ζ, op hε hζ a c ∈[hδ] x ∧
      u = op hγ hδ (singleton hε (singleton hζ a)) (op hε hζ b c)} hβ ?_
  · obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := this
    use y
    intro a b c
    rw [hy]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨a', b', c', h₁, h₂⟩
      simp only [op_inj, singleton_inj] at h₂
      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩ := h₂
      exact h₁
    · intro h
      exact ⟨a, b, c, h, rfl⟩
  · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_support x
    use S ↗ hγ ↗ hβ
    intro ρ hρ
    simp only [Support.smul_scoderiv, Support.scoderiv_inj, ← allPermSderiv_forget'] at hρ
    specialize hS (ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ) hρ
    ext z
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, ⟨a, b, c, hx, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε ↘ hζ • a, ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε ↘ hζ • b,
        ρ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε ↘ hζ • c, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [← hS]
        simp only [mem_smul_iff', allPerm_inv_sderiv', smul_op, inv_smul_smul]
        exact hx
      · simp only [smul_op, smul_singleton]
    · rintro ⟨a, b, c, hx, rfl⟩
      rw [Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem]
      refine ⟨ρ⁻¹ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε ↘ hζ • a, ρ⁻¹ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε ↘ hζ • b,
        ρ⁻¹ ↘ hβ ↘ hγ ↘ hδ ↘ hε ↘ hζ • c, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [smul_eq_iff_eq_inv_smul] at hS
        rw [hS, mem_smul_iff']
        simp only [inv_inv, allPerm_inv_sderiv', smul_op, smul_inv_smul]
        exact hx
      · simp only [smul_op, allPerm_inv_sderiv', smul_singleton]

    {x : TSet β} {y : TSet α} (h : β < α) (ρ : AllPerm α) :
    x ∈[h] ρ • y ↔ ρ⁻¹ ↘ h • x ∈[h] y := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α.recBotCoe (Nonempty.some inferInstance) id⟩
  letI : LeLevel α := ⟨α.recBotCoe (λ _ ↦ bot_le) (λ _ h ↦ WithBot.coe_le_coe.mpr h.le)

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

theorem TSet.exists_of_symmetric {α β : Λ} (s : Set (TSet β)) (hβ : (β : TypeIndex) < α)
    (hs : Symmetric s hβ) :
    ∃ x : TSet α, ∀ y : TSet β, y ∈[hβ] x ↔ y ∈ s := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  letI : LtLevel β := ⟨hβ⟩
  suffices ∃ x : (@TSet _ α newModelData.toPreModelData), ∀ y : TSet β, yᵁ ∈[hβ] xᵁ ↔ y ∈ s by
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
    use newSetEquiv x
    intro y
    rw [← hx, ← TSet.forget_mem_forget, newSetEquiv_forget]
  obtain rfl | hs' := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · use none
    intro y
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    exact not_mem_none y
  · use some (Code.toSet ⟨β, s, hs'⟩ ?_)
    · intro y
      erw [mem_some_iff]
      exact Code.mem_toSet _
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hs
      use S
      intro ρ hρS
      have := hS (allPermEquiv ρ) ?_
      · simp only [NewPerm.smul_mk, Code.mk.injEq, heq_eq_eq, true_and]
        rwa [allPermEquiv_sderiv] at this
      · rwa [allPermEquiv_forget]

theorem exists_inter (x y : TSet α) :
    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {z | z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := symmetric y hβ
  use S + T
  intro ρ hρ
  specialize hS ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS hT ⊢
  aesop

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

    ∃ S : Support α, ∀ ρ : AllPerm α, ρᵁ • S = S → ρ • x = x := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := NewSet.exists_support (newSetEquiv.symm x)
  use S
  intro ρ hρ
  have := @Support.Supports.supports _ _ _ newPreModelData _ _ _ hS (allPermEquiv.symm ρ) ?_
  · apply tSetForget_injective
    have := congr_arg (·ᵁ) this
    simp only at this
    erw [@smul_forget _ _ newModelData (allPermEquiv.symm ρ) (newSetEquiv.symm x),
      ← allPermEquiv_forget, ← newSetEquiv_forget, Equiv.apply_symm_apply,
      Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at this
    rwa [smul_forget]
  · rwa [← allPermEquiv_forget, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩

    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
    use newSetEquiv x
    intro y
    rw [← hx, ← TSet.forget_mem_forget, newSetEquiv_forget]
  obtain rfl | hs' := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · use none
    intro y
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    exact not_mem_none y
  · use some (Code.toSet ⟨β, s, hs'⟩ ?_)
    · intro y

      exact Code.mem_toSet _
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hs

        rwa [allPermEquiv_sderiv] at this

informal_statement: For any typed set \( x \) in \( TSet(\gamma) \), there exists a typed set \( y \) in \( TSet(\alpha) \) such that for every element \( a \), \( a \) is in \( y \) under the condition \( h\beta \) if and only if there exist elements \( b \) and \( c \) where \( a \) can be expressed as \( op(h\gamma, h\delta)(b, c) \) and \( c \) is in \( x \) under the condition \( h\delta \).
informal_proof:
We start by considering an arbitrary element \( x \) in \( TSet(\gamma) \). Our goal is to construct an appropriate set \( y \) in \( TSet(\alpha) \) that satisfies the stated condition.

First, we utilize the symmetric nature of set operations to define \( y \) as a transformation of a support set derived from \( x \). Specifically, we obtain a support set \( S \) associated with \( x \) and define \( y \) using this support set along with the given conditions \( h\gamma \) and \( h\beta \).

To establish the equivalence, we proceed in two directions:

1. **Forward Direction (\( \Rightarrow \)):**  
   Assume \( a \) is in \( y \) under condition \( h\beta \). By definition, this means there exist elements \( b \) and \( c \) such that \( a = op(h\gamma, h\delta)(b, c) \) and \( c \) is in \( x \) under condition \( h\delta \). This directly satisfies the required condition.

2. **Reverse Direction (\( \Leftarrow \)):**  
   Conversely, if \( a = op(h\gamma, h\delta)(b, c) \) for some \( b \) and \( c \), and \( c \) is in \( x \) under \( h\delta \), then by the construction of \( y \), \( a \) must be in \( y \) under \( h\beta \).

By satisfying both directions, we have demonstrated the existence of such a set \( y \) that fulfills the stated condition.

theorem exists_inter (x y : TSet α) :
    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {z | z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := symmetric y hβ
  use S + T
  intro ρ hρ
  specialize hS ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS hT ⊢
  aesop

theorem exists_compl (x : TSet α) :
    ∃ y : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] y ↔ ¬z ∈[hβ] x := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {z | ¬z ∈[hβ] x} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ
  use S
  intro ρ hρ
  specialize hS ρ hρ
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS ⊢
  aesop

theorem exists_up (x y : TSet β) :
    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z = x ∨ z = y := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {x, y} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_support x
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := exists_support y
  use (S + T) ↗ hβ
  intro ρ hρ
  rw [Support.smul_scoderiv, Support.scoderiv_inj, ← allPermSderiv_forget'] at hρ
  specialize hS (ρ ↘ hβ) (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT (ρ ↘ hβ) (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp only [Set.smul_set_def, Set.image, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
    exists_eq_or_imp, hS, exists_eq_left, hT]
  ext z
  rw [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  aesop

/-- The unordered pair. -/
def up (x y : TSet β) : TSet α :=
  (exists_up hβ x y).choose

@[simp]
theorem mem_up_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    z ∈[hβ] up hβ x y ↔ z = x ∨ z = y :=
  (exists_up hβ x y).choose_spec z

/-- The Kuratowski ordered pair. -/
def op (x y : TSet γ) : TSet α :=
  up hβ (singleton hγ x) (up hγ x y)

theorem up_injective {x y z w : TSet β} (h : up hβ x y = up hβ z w) :
    (x = z ∧ y = w) ∨ (x = w ∧ y = z) := by
  have h₁ := mem_up_iff hβ x y z
  have h₂ := mem_up_iff hβ x y w
  have h₃ := mem_up_iff hβ z w x
  have h₄ := mem_up_iff hβ z w y
  rw [h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
  rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₃ h₄
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_inj (x y z w : TSet β) :
    up hβ x y = up hβ z w ↔ (x = z ∧ y = w) ∨ (x = w ∧ y = z) := by
  constructor
  · exact up_injective hβ
  · rintro (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
    · rfl
    · apply tSet_ext' hβ
      aesop

theorem up_self {x : TSet β} :
    up hβ x x = singleton hβ x := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  aesop

    up hβ x y = singleton hβ z ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h₁ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z x
    have h₂ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z y
    rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
    aesop
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rw [up_self]

    singleton hβ z = up hβ x y ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  rw [← up_eq_singleton_iff hβ x y z, eq_comm]

    x = z ∧ y = w := by
  rw [op, op] at h
  simp only [up_inj, singleton_inj, singleton_eq_up_iff, up_eq_singleton_iff] at h
  obtain (⟨rfl, ⟨h, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨h, rfl⟩⟩) := h <;> simp only [and_self]

  rintro rfl
  simp only [up_eq_singleton_iff, true_and, singleton_inj]

theorem up_self {x : TSet β} :
    up hβ x x = singleton hβ x := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_eq_singleton_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    up hβ x y = singleton hβ z ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h₁ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z x

    rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
    aesop
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rw [up_self]

@[simp]
theorem singleton_eq_up_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    singleton hβ z = up hβ x y ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  rw [← up_eq_singleton_iff hβ x y z, eq_comm]

theorem op_injective {x y z w : TSet γ} (h : op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ z w) :
    x = z ∧ y = w := by
  rw [op, op] at h
  simp only [up_inj, singleton_inj, singleton_eq_up_iff, up_eq_singleton_iff] at h
  obtain (⟨rfl, ⟨h, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨h, rfl⟩⟩) := h <;> simp only [and_self]

@[simp]
theorem op_inj (x y z w : TSet γ) :
    op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ z w ↔ x = z ∧ y = w := by
  constructor
  · exact op_injective hβ hγ
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rfl

  rintro rfl
  simp only [up_eq_singleton_iff, true_and, singleton_inj]

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

theorem TSet.exists_support {α : Λ} (x : TSet α) :
    ∃ S : Support α, ∀ ρ : AllPerm α, ρᵁ • S = S → ρ • x = x := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := NewSet.exists_support (newSetEquiv.symm x)
  use S
  intro ρ hρ
  have := @Support.Supports.supports _ _ _ newPreModelData _ _ _ hS (allPermEquiv.symm ρ) ?_
  · apply tSetForget_injective
    have := congr_arg (·ᵁ) this
    simp only at this
    erw [@smul_forget _ _ newModelData (allPermEquiv.symm ρ) (newSetEquiv.symm x),
      ← allPermEquiv_forget, ← newSetEquiv_forget, Equiv.apply_symm_apply,
      Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at this
    rwa [smul_forget]
  · rwa [← allPermEquiv_forget, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

theorem TSet.exists_of_symmetric {α β : Λ} (s : Set (TSet β)) (hβ : (β : TypeIndex) < α)
    (hs : Symmetric s hβ) :
    ∃ x : TSet α, ∀ y : TSet β, y ∈[hβ] x ↔ y ∈ s := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  letI : LtLevel β := ⟨hβ⟩
  suffices ∃ x : (@TSet _ α newModelData.toPreModelData), ∀ y : TSet β, yᵁ ∈[hβ] xᵁ ↔ y ∈ s by
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
    use newSetEquiv x
    intro y
    rw [← hx, ← TSet.forget_mem_forget, newSetEquiv_forget]
  obtain rfl | hs' := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · use none
    intro y
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    exact not_mem_none y
  · use some (Code.toSet ⟨β, s, hs'⟩ ?_)
    · intro y
      erw [mem_some_iff]
      exact Code.mem_toSet _
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hs
      use S
      intro ρ hρS
      have := hS (allPermEquiv ρ) ?_
      · simp only [NewPerm.smul_mk, Code.mk.injEq, heq_eq_eq, true_and]
        rwa [allPermEquiv_sderiv] at this
      · rwa [allPermEquiv_forget]

theorem exists_inter (x y : TSet α) :
    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y := by
  refine exists_of_symmetric {z | z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y} hβ ?_
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := symmetric y hβ
  use S + T
  intro ρ hρ
  specialize hS ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS hT ⊢
  aesop

theorem up_injective {x y z w : TSet β} (h : up hβ x y = up hβ z w) :
    (x = z ∧ y = w) ∨ (x = w ∧ y = z) := by
  have h₁ := mem_up_iff hβ x y z
  have h₂ := mem_up_iff hβ x y w
  have h₃ := mem_up_iff hβ z w x
  have h₄ := mem_up_iff hβ z w y
  rw [h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
  rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₃ h₄
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_inj (x y z w : TSet β) :
    up hβ x y = up hβ z w ↔ (x = z ∧ y = w) ∨ (x = w ∧ y = z) := by
  constructor
  · exact up_injective hβ
  · rintro (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
    · rfl
    · apply tSet_ext' hβ
      aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_self {x : TSet β} :
    up hβ x x = singleton hβ x := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  aesop

@[simp]
theorem up_eq_singleton_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    up hβ x y = singleton hβ z ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h₁ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z x
    have h₂ := typedMem_singleton_iff' hβ z y
    rw [← h, mem_up_iff] at h₁ h₂
    aesop
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rw [up_self]

@[simp]
theorem singleton_eq_up_iff (x y z : TSet β) :
    singleton hβ z = up hβ x y ↔ x = z ∧ y = z := by
  rw [← up_eq_singleton_iff hβ x y z, eq_comm]

theorem op_injective {x y z w : TSet γ} (h : op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ z w) :
    x = z ∧ y = w := by
  rw [op, op] at h
  simp only [up_inj, singleton_inj, singleton_eq_up_iff, up_eq_singleton_iff] at h
  obtain (⟨rfl, ⟨h, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩⟩ | ⟨⟨rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨h, rfl⟩⟩) := h <;> simp only [and_self]

@[simp]
theorem op_inj (x y z w : TSet γ) :
    op hβ hγ x y = op hβ hγ z w ↔ x = z ∧ y = w := by
  constructor
  · exact op_injective hβ hγ
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rfl

@[simp]
theorem op_eq_singleton_iff (x y : TSet γ) (z : TSet β) :
    op hβ hγ x y = singleton hβ z ↔ singleton hγ x = z ∧ singleton hγ y = z := by
  rw [op, up_eq_singleton_iff, and_congr_right_iff]
  rintro rfl
  simp only [up_eq_singleton_iff, true_and, singleton_inj]

@[simp]
theorem smul_up (x y : TSet β) (ρ : AllPerm α) :
    ρ • up hβ x y = up hβ (ρ ↘ hβ • x) (ρ ↘ hβ • y) := by
  apply tSet_ext' hβ
  aesop

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

    ∃ x : TSet α, ∀ y : TSet β, y ∈[hβ] x ↔ y ∈ s := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  letI : LtLevel β := ⟨hβ⟩
  suffices ∃ x : (@TSet _ α newModelData.toPreModelData), ∀ y : TSet β, yᵁ ∈[hβ] xᵁ ↔ y ∈ s by
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
    use newSetEquiv x
    intro y
    rw [← hx, ← TSet.forget_mem_forget, newSetEquiv_forget]
  obtain rfl | hs' := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · use none
    intro y
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    exact not_mem_none y
  · use some (Code.toSet ⟨β, s, hs'⟩ ?_)
    · intro y

      exact Code.mem_toSet _
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hs

      intro ρ hρS
      have := hS (allPermEquiv ρ) ?_
      · simp only [NewPerm.smul_mk, Code.mk.injEq, heq_eq_eq, true_and]
        rwa [allPermEquiv_sderiv] at this
      · rwa [allPermEquiv_forget]

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

theorem TSet.exists_of_symmetric {α β : Λ} (s : Set (TSet β)) (hβ : (β : TypeIndex) < α)
    (hs : Symmetric s hβ) :
    ∃ x : TSet α, ∀ y : TSet β, y ∈[hβ] x ↔ y ∈ s := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  letI : LtLevel β := ⟨hβ⟩
  suffices ∃ x : (@TSet _ α newModelData.toPreModelData), ∀ y : TSet β, yᵁ ∈[hβ] xᵁ ↔ y ∈ s by
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
    use newSetEquiv x
    intro y
    rw [← hx, ← TSet.forget_mem_forget, newSetEquiv_forget]
  obtain rfl | hs' := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · use none
    intro y
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    exact not_mem_none y
  · use some (Code.toSet ⟨β, s, hs'⟩ ?_)
    · intro y
      erw [mem_some_iff]
      exact Code.mem_toSet _
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hs
      use S
      intro ρ hρS
      have := hS (allPermEquiv ρ) ?_
      · simp only [NewPerm.smul_mk, Code.mk.injEq, heq_eq_eq, true_and]
        rwa [allPermEquiv_sderiv] at this
      · rwa [allPermEquiv_forget]

  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS hT ⊢
  aesop

informal_statement: For any set \( x \), there exists a set \( y \) such that for any set \( z \), \( z \) belongs to \( y \) if and only if \( z \) does not belong to \( x \) under the relation \( h\beta \).
informal_proof:
To prove this statement, we start by considering the set of all elements that do not belong to \( x \) under the relation \( h\beta \). Let's denote this set as \( S \), where
\[ S = \{ z \mid \lnot(z \in_{h\beta} x) \} \]

We aim to show that this set \( S \) serves as the complement of \( x \) with respect to \( h\beta \). To do this, we need to demonstrate that for any set \( \rho \), \( \rho \) belongs to \( S \) if and only if \( \rho \) does not belong to \( x \).

First, assume that \( \rho \) is an element of \( S \). By the definition of \( S \), this means:
\[ \rho \in_{h\beta} S \iff \rho \in_{h\beta} \{ z \mid \lnot(z \in_{h\beta} x) \} \]

Since \( \rho \) satisfies the membership condition of \( S \), it implies that:
\[ \rho \not\in_{h\beta} x \]

Conversely, if \( \rho \) does not belong to \( x \), then by the definition of \( S \), \( \rho \) must be an element of \( S \):
\[ \rho \not\in_{h\beta} x \implies \rho \in_{h\beta} S \]

Thus, we have established the equivalence:
\[ \rho \in_{h\beta} S \iff \rho \not\in_{h\beta} x \]

Therefore, the set \( S \) satisfies the condition to be the complement of \( x \) with respect to \( h\beta \), proving the existence of such a complement.

theorem TSet.exists_of_symmetric {α β : Λ} (s : Set (TSet β)) (hβ : (β : TypeIndex) < α)
    (hs : Symmetric s hβ) :
    ∃ x : TSet α, ∀ y : TSet β, y ∈[hβ] x ↔ y ∈ s := by
  letI : Level := ⟨α⟩
  letI : LtLevel β := ⟨hβ⟩
  suffices ∃ x : (@TSet _ α newModelData.toPreModelData), ∀ y : TSet β, yᵁ ∈[hβ] xᵁ ↔ y ∈ s by
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
    use newSetEquiv x
    intro y
    rw [← hx, ← TSet.forget_mem_forget, newSetEquiv_forget]
  obtain rfl | hs' := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · use none
    intro y
    simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    exact not_mem_none y
  · use some (Code.toSet ⟨β, s, hs'⟩ ?_)
    · intro y
      erw [mem_some_iff]
      exact Code.mem_toSet _
    · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := hs
      use S
      intro ρ hρS
      have := hS (allPermEquiv ρ) ?_
      · simp only [NewPerm.smul_mk, Code.mk.injEq, heq_eq_eq, true_and]
        rwa [allPermEquiv_sderiv] at this
      · rwa [allPermEquiv_forget]

    ∃ w : TSet α, ∀ z : TSet β, z ∈[hβ] w ↔ z ∈[hβ] x ∧ z ∈[hβ] y := by

  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := symmetric x hβ

  specialize hS ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_right hρ)
  specialize hT ρ (smul_eq_of_le Support.le_add_left hρ)
  simp [Set.ext_iff, Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem] at hS hT ⊢
  aesop
